Definition: Whether the instant payment system supports business payments to suppliers, vendors, contractors, and other businesses for commercial transactions, procurement, and supply chain payments.
Comments: B2B payments functionality is supported via the banking and interoperable payment ecosystem (GIMACPAY includes transfer services for participants such as banks, payment institutions, and public treasuries), but public evidence tying this explicitly to a B2B use case in Cameroon is limited, so scored conservatively.

Comments: P2B payments are available via mobile money and GIMACPAY’s merchant/QR ecosystem (e.g., GIMACPAY QR code payments under MaDigiPaie enabling citizens to pay purchases via mobile money apps regardless of operator).

Comments: P2P is widely available via mobile money (e.g., MTN Mobile Money and Orange Money), and interoperable transfers are supported in the GIMACPAY ecosystem (card/mobile/transfer interoperability across participants).

Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: BEAC directly operates/oversees core payment infrastructure and settlement (SYGMA RTGS; payment systems oversight) and is the dominant owner/settlement agent for GIMACPAY governance, indicating strong central-bank governance.

Definition: Whether national data protection or privacy legislation exists and explicitly covers payment transaction data, including provisions on data collection, storage, sharing, retention, and user rights over their payment data.
Comments: General privacy/data protection exists via Cameroon’s Law No. 2010/012 on Cybersecurity and Cybercrime (general protections around data/security), but no clear payments-specific data privacy law was evidenced in the materials reviewed.

Definition: Whether payment system governance explicitly includes mechanisms to ensure inclusivity and represent interests of vulnerable populations, including provisions for input from all participant types, consumer representatives, small providers, or explicit financial inclusion mandates in governance documents.
Comments: Pro-poor/inclusion governance exists but is partial: Cameroon’s National Strategy for Inclusive Finance (SNFI 2023–2027) targets vulnerable groups (rural populations, women, youth, MSMEs), and the BEAC-led CNEF performs consumer protection/mediation functions, but there is limited evidence of a comprehensive, enforceable pro-poor governance framework specific to instant payments scheme governance.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing an instant/real-time payment system (IPS/RTP) that enables digital payments with near-instant settlement (typically within seconds), available 24/7/365. This includes both bank-led and mobile money interoperability systems.
Comments: GIMACPAY (GIMAC interoperable instant payments ecosystem under BEAC oversight) has been live since July 2020 and provides real-time clearing for payments across CEMAC including Cameroon, with settlement via BEAC’s SYGMA RTGS, meeting “fully deployed” digital payments infrastructure criteria.
